PERSONAL / SOFTGOODS / CASE STUDY 09

Outseam-Panel Flared Jeans

Reshape the lower leg by inserting reclaimed denim panels into the outseams while retaining the existing waist and upper fit.

Project type
Personal project
Role
Designer & Maker
Timeline
2024–2025
Exact completion month was not recorded.
Disciplines
Softgoods design / Pattern development / Prototyping
Status
Completed
01 Problem02 Requirements03 Concepts04 Pattern Geometry05 Design06 Build / Test07 Results08 What I Learned
01

Problem

I wanted a more pronounced flared silhouette while keeping the original waist and upper fit of an existing pair of jeans.

I added denim to the outseams, using reclaimed material and a triangular panel approach to increase the lower-leg opening.

02

Requirements

RequirementEngineering definition
FitRetain the existing approximately 28 × 30 base garment.
Panel placementOne added outseam panel per leg.
Seam allowance0.5 in.
FinishCreate a matched flared silhouette across both legs.
03

Concepts

ITERATION / 01

Draft the panel

Use a cardboard template to explore the triangle geometry and transfer a matched shape onto donor denim.

ITERATION / 02

Fit the added volume

Open the outseam and position each insert so the added width grows toward the hem.

04

Pattern Geometry

Pattern dimensions below are estimates; seam allowance is 0.5 in.

Finished insert geometry: 16 in height and 6 in width at the hem seam line. Starting from a 7.5 in laid-flat hem width (15 in circumference), one 6 in insert per leg increases the finished laid-flat width to approximately 10.5 in (21 in circumference).

Offset each sloping stitch line and the hem by 0.5 in. The mitered cut outline is approximately 7.21 in wide and 19.21 in high. Truncate the sharp tip as needed for construction.

05

Design

The triangular insert introduces additional width gradually, concentrating the silhouette change at the lower leg.

I used the existing garment as the base and donor denim for the inserts, with a 0.5-inch allowance for joining the panels.

06

Build / Test

The photos show material planning, a cardboard template, the laid-flat assembly, and the finished jeans worn.

The final wear photo shows the resulting flare and drape.

07

Results

The jeans gained a flared lower-leg silhouette through added outseam panels. The photographs document the completed garment.

2outseam inserts, one per leg
0.5 inseam allowance
Retainedoriginal waist and upper fit
08

What I Learned

Panel shape controls where volume appears. Working from a base garment made it important to balance the two legs and evaluate the drape in wear, not just on the floor.
